title: Playground Playtest + Failure Mode Walkthrough
summary: Introductory sandbox/demo of Redwood hosted generation APIs and Console 'Playground' with emphasis on streaming behavior, param tuning, and retry/fallback patterns. Customer concerned about tail latency, data retention, and on-prem failover; SE ran live playtest, showed console suggestions and Redwood Optimize hints. Agreed next steps include trial project, security pack, and baseline perf test in early Jan.
topics: KV cache and prefix caching mention
next_steps: Redwood: Share sandbox link + sample prompt set (Maya) - by 2026-12-22
Customer: Provide sample conversational transcripts and success criteria (Lena) - by 2027-01-05
Redwood SE: Schedule 1-hr perf baseline with SRE (Samir) - week of 2027-01-09
action_items: Maya Patel: Send hosted sandbox link and quickstart snippets - due 2026-12-22
Ethan Chu: Prepare perf checklist and benchmark script for NovaPay - due 2027-01-07
Priya Mehta: Share 3 representative prompt sets and expected latency targets - due 2027-01-05
transcript:
[00:00:00] Maya: hi everyone thanks for joining really appreciate you making time today, this is Maya from Redwood inference, i'm joined by Ethan and Diego from our engineering team. how's everyone doing?
[00:00:08] Lena: good thanks, excited to see the playground. we chatted a bit over email about latency targets and data retention.
[00:00:15] Maya: yes exactly, our goal today is a hands-on playtest of the hosted generation playground, show streaming behavior, go through params like temperature and top_p, and then cover retry/fallbacks and what happens if the hosted path degrades. we'll also point to the Console Optimize hints. sound good?
[00:00:28] Samir: yep that's what i care about — tail latency and how retries impact cost.
[00:00:32] Ethan: perfect, i'll kick off the live session, and please interrupt if anything looks off, sometimes the transcription guesses words weirdly.
[00:00:40] [screen share starts]
[00:00:44] Ethan: ok i'm on the Redwood Console Playground, creating a new chat session, selecting the hosted-chat endpoint and a mid-size open model. first thing — streaming toggle on. you'll notice the UI streams partial tokens as they arrive, so apps can render typing effects without waiting for finalization.
[00:01:02] Priya: is streaming using chunked transfer or SSE?
[00:01:05] Ethan: behind the scenes it's chunked HTTP with server-sent event semantics for the SDKs. small mismatch in wording sometimes but that is the transport. it allows incremental deltas and early rendering.
[00:01:16] Diego: also note our SDKs expose on_partial callbacks so you can suppress updates until X tokens or time thresholds. that's helpful for UI jitter.
[00:01:26] Arjun: what happens if the stream drops mid-response?
[00:01:28] Ethan: good q — default behavior is an automatic retry, we attempt idempotent resume by replaying the prompt plus the partial state when possible. if the model variant doesn't support resume we fall back to returning a final generation from a compatible model variant and annotate the response with a fallback reason.
[00:01:46] Samir: so cost implications? retries and full regenerations will bump token usage, right?
[00:01:51] Maya: yes, worst-case you pay for the extra tokens for retries; that's why we demonstrate backoff and resume so you minimize re-generation. Optimize suggests session-specific caching and prefix caching to reduce cost for repeated prefixes.
[00:02:05] [00:02:05] Lena: can you show an end-to-end example where streaming glitches and how resume plays out?
[00:02:10] Ethan: sure i'll force a simulated network hiccup in the playground. watch the token stream pause... pause... okay now it timed out, you can see in the console a retry kicked and the SDK re-requested with resume token. here it resumes at token 48 and completes.
[00:02:31] Priya: transcription note - 'resume token' sometimes shows up as 'Rz token' in our logs, that's ok.
[00:02:36] Diego: also the Console shows the latency histogram and per-token breakdown, that helps catch if a particular chunk is slow due to kernel selection or long-loop ops.
[00:02:48] [00:03:00] Ethan: switching now to parameter tuning — temperature 0.0, 0.7, 1.0 quick side-by-side so you can see diversity differences.
[00:03:10] Lena: nice. in our product we need concise, deterministic replies for receipts and a more creative mode for marketing messages, so we might switch contextually.
[00:03:20] Ethan: exactly, we suggest two approaches — keep one model with dynamic params, or use lightweight routing to different model variants for deterministic vs creative. routing adds operational overhead but gives clearer bounds on output quality.
[00:03:34] Samir: the routing approach — does Redwood handle that or do we need to implement in our app?
[00:03:38] Maya: Redwood can do policy-based routing in the control plane — you set a rule to route to a low-temp variant for certain endpoints or tokens. it's in the Console under 'Routing policies'.
[00:03:48] Priya: ok if we pick policy routing we still need SLO observability for switched paths, right?
[00:03:53] Diego: yes we emit traces and per-route perf metrics; you can attach tracing headers from your app to link requests back to logs.
[00:04:02] [00:04:15] Ethan: quick note about tokenization: for cost predictability use the Console's token estimator. we just pasted a sample prompt and it estimated ~38 tokens, but edge cases exist for emoji and non-ascii.
[00:04:28] Lena: are there examples for safe retry parameters? like how many retries and backoff curve?
[00:04:33] Ethan: default is 2 retries with exponential backoff starting at 250ms, capped at 2s. we often suggest 1 retry for latency-critical endpoints and more retries for throughput-orientated batch tasks. Optimize can recommend tuning based on past failure distribution.
[00:04:49] Samir: do we get chargebacks or detailed token-level billing to understand retry cost?
[00:04:54] Maya: yes console shows per-request token breakdown and you can export usage per-route and per-api-key to your billing dashboard.
[00:05:02] [00:05:10] Lena: let's pivot to security — we are regulated, need SOC2 and KMS support and audit trails.
[00:05:15] Maya: Redwood has SOC2 and supports customer-managed keys via KMS/HSM for Private deployments; hosted has encrypted-at-rest and key rotation. Console exposes audit logs for API calls; we can share the security pack PDF.
[00:05:28] Arjun: and data retention? we need data purging and no retention beyond 30 days unless specified.
[00:05:33] Diego: hosted defaults to short retention but you can request a retention policy. Dedicated and Private give you full control. we'll attach the policy options.
[00:05:42] [00:06:00] Ethan: ok back to playtest — i'll run a prompt set that includes a multi-turn conversation with a repeated prefix to show prefix caching. watch throughput improvement on repeat.
[00:06:12] Priya: i see a 40% token/time improvement on second run — is that the KV cache kicking in?
[00:06:18] Ethan: yes, prefix KV cache reduced compute for earlier layers. Optimize flagged this pattern and suggested enabling prefix caching for that route.
[00:06:27] Samir: curious about private deployment failover — if we run a Private on-prem with a hybrid fallback to hosted, how seamless is that?
[00:06:34] Maya: it's a policy you set — primary private cluster with fallback to hosted variants. in an outage, requests route to hosted and you get annotated fallbacks. there are security considerations and data egress implications we can discuss with your security team.
[00:06:47] Lena: any customers done this hybrid setup?
[00:06:50] Diego: yes a payments company used Private for PII workloads and hosted for non-PII fallback; they ran a canary for fallbacks and Redwood's routing kept latency impact within their SLOs.
[00:07:02] [00:07:15] Ethan: i'm going to purposely change the model to a quantized variant to show differences in token time and slight variance in output.
[00:07:23] Priya: output looks slightly terser. is that expected?
[00:07:26] Ethan: yes quantization can affect response shape; Optimize produces quality deltas so you can decide acceptable tradeoffs.
[00:07:34] Samir: what about cold-start token latency for large context loads?
[00:07:38] Diego: we measure first-token-latency and show warm vs cold histograms. for cold starts we recommend pinned warm pools for high-sla endpoints. that is part of the Dedicated offering.
[00:07:50] [00:08:10] Lena: can you drop a link to the benchmark sheet you mentioned earlier?
[00:08:13] Maya: sure dropping link in chat: https://redwood.example/sandbox/nova-playtest (note: demo link). also the perf spreadsheet is attached in the follow-up email.
[00:08:24] [00:09:00] Priya: quick question about SDK behavior: our mobile app uses intermittent networks — any patterns to reduce partial duplicates when reconnecting?
[00:09:07] Ethan: for mobile, enable low-timer partial buffering and client-side de-dupe using the request id. the SDK sets a stable request_id header you can store; on reconnect you can ask for delta since last ack.
[00:09:21] Arjun: do you provide sample mobile adapters?
[00:09:24] Diego: yes we have sample adapters for iOS/Android in our docs repo.
[00:09:30] [00:10:00] Ethan: let's intentionally cause a model overload to see fallback policy — toggling concurrency low... sending burst of 20 requests. you'll see some requests route to lower-cost variant and others queue based on policy.
[00:10:18] Lena: i see a few responses labelled 'fallback-model' in the console, and a small increase in latency but not failures.
[00:10:23] Samir: excellent — we care more about availability than absolute latency.
[00:10:28] Maya: that's a key tradeoff we see in payments workflows: prefer graceful degradation instead of errors.
[00:10:33] [00:11:00] Priya: wanted to ask about safety filters and prompt-moderation, do you recommend doing it client-side or using Redwood's moderation?
[00:11:07] Ethan: we provide an integrated moderation pipeline you can opt into — it runs a fast classifier pre-generation to filter or flag content. many customers use both: Redwood moderation for quick blocking and additional app logic for business rules.
[00:11:20] Lena: can we run moderation in our private stack?
[00:11:23] Diego: yes for Private and Dedicated you can run local moderation models or route to hosted moderation with encrypted payloads.
[00:11:30] [00:12:00] Ethan: stamping through notes — we'll capture the console screenshots, the playground prompts we used, and the Optimize recommendations.
[00:12:08] Lena: one last operational question: can we set per-tenant rate-limits and quotas? we have internal teams and external partners.
[00:12:14] Maya: yes per-api-key quotas, per-route caps, and token budgets by org are supported. we also offer alerts if spend or error rates exceed thresholds.
[00:12:25] Samir: ok that's helpful.
[00:12:30] [00:13:00] Ethan: wrapping up demo — quick recap: showed streaming and resume, parameter tuning, prefix caching, fallback routing, and how Optimize gives tuning hints.
[00:13:09] Lena: thanks, very practical. next steps for us will be to run a small pilot and have a perf baseline.
[00:13:15] Maya: perfect — we'll send the sandbox link and the perf script, and Ethan will coordinate the baseline with Samir.
[00:13:21] Arjun: any pricing ballpark for hosted vs dedicated for our expected 10M tokens/month?
[00:13:26] Maya: i'll share a ballpark in the follow-up. Hosted is usage-based; Dedicated is reserved capacity — we'll outline both with examples.
[00:13:33] Priya: would like to see a cost example with and without retries in that spreadsheet.
[00:13:38] Diego: we'll add a column showing retry-induced cost delta.
[00:13:42] [00:14:00] Maya: thanks again everyone, we'll follow up with the items in chat. anything else before we close?
[00:14:07] Lena: no that's it for me, great session.
[00:14:10] Samir: thanks all.
[00:14:15] [call ends with screen share]
notes: Transcription contains occasional mis-heard tokens and shortened timestamps; speaker labels are from fireflies autopopulate. Links were shared in chat during demo. The team agreed to a Jan perf baseline and a pilot. Security pack and pricing follow-up promised.
